Transaction-aware account lookup and modification helpers with fork tracking and record publishing.

# Purpose
This C file implements account database access on top of the `fd_funk` transaction and record system. It provides the user lifecycle functions [`fd_accdb_user_join`](<#fd_accdb_user_join>) and [`fd_accdb_user_leave`](<#fd_accdb_user_leave>), then uses transaction fork tracking to bind an `fd_accdb_user_t` handle to a specific transaction XID. The code loads the active fork with [`fd_accdb_load_fork`](<#fd_accdb_load_fork>) and [`fd_accdb_load_fork_slow`](<#fd_accdb_load_fork_slow>), checks fork membership with [`fd_accdb_has_xid`](<#fd_accdb_has_xid>), and searches record chains with [`fd_accdb_search_chain`](<#fd_accdb_search_chain>) and [`fd_accdb_peek1`](<#fd_accdb_peek1>) to find the current account record for a given address.

The file also implements account modification support. [`fd_accdb_modify_prepare`](<#fd_accdb_modify_prepare>) selects the correct fork, checks transaction state, and prepares either a new record, an in-place update, or a copy-on-write update for a frozen record. Helper functions such as [`fd_accdb_prep_create`](<#fd_accdb_prep_create>), [`fd_accdb_prep_inplace`](<#fd_accdb_prep_inplace>), and [`fd_accdb_copy_account`](<#fd_accdb_copy_account>) set up record metadata and data buffers. The write path ends with [`fd_accdb_write_publish`](<#fd_accdb_write_publish>), which publishes a prepared record into the transaction record list and updates the active write reference count.
